subject: ventures/ppf-ceramic-coating-price-calculator
professional: an auto-detailing shop owner who installs paint protection film and ceramic coatings and sets the shop's package menu; first checks: linear feet of 60 in film per coverage and vehicle (roll yield, waste), install hours per panel package, correction stage hours, bay days including cure, margin vs markup, and whether the 'which package to sell' advice reflects what the market pays rather than what the job costs

evidence.correctness: Recomputed four jobs with an independent Python script (python3 -I indep.py, written from the page's stated method, not from calc.mjs) and compared with plan(): A sample sedan full front + coating + stage 1: 24.15 tech h, 4 work days, 5 bay days, cost $2,364.01, price $3,940.02 (= cost/0.6, margin not markup), $315.20/bay day; B truck full body, no coating, stage 2, 2 techs: 73.5 h, 5 days, $6,137.50, $10,229.17, $818.33; C SUV coating only, 2 cure days: 3 bay days, $658.75, $1,097.92; D compact partial, no coating: $853.40, $1,422.33. All match to the cent. By hand for A: film 24 x 1.15 = 27.6 ft, x 1.15 waste = 31.74 ft x $24 = $761.76; labour 24.15 x 35 = $845.25; overhead 5 x 120 = $600; redo 0.06 x 450 = $27; + 90 + 40 = $2,364.01. Arithmetic is right; the defects are in what it recommends (domain) and in silent zero defaults: a blank labour rate or film cost silently prices with $0 labour/film (plan({...s, laborRate:''}).job.labor = 0). Display rounds 24.15 tech hours to 24.1 (float, round1 + EPSILON too small).
evidence.completeness: README features checked against plan() output: film footage by package and size with waste (yes), install/correction/coating hours (yes), work days and cure days as bay days (yes), bay overhead (yes), expected redo (yes), margin as share of price (yes), minimum charge (yes, test passes), every package side by side with profit per bay day (yes), redo sensitivity 0/3/6/12/20% (yes), share link round-trip (yes), CSV (yes). No stubs or TODOs. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin left in llms.txt, sitemap, robots, canonicals. Live host returned proxy 403 (curl: CONNECT tunnel failed, 403).
evidence.verification: cd ventures/ppf-ceramic-coating-price-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 25 pass, 0 fail. Only one test pins exact numbers (the sample job); the rest are inequalities. Five mutants via quality_mutate.py: correction not scaled by size caught; margin -> markup caught; cure day applied without coating caught; minimum-charge boundary moved SURVIVED; 'best package' ranked by price instead of profit per bay day SURVIVED (the headline recommendation is unpinned; under cost-plus pricing the two rankings coincide on the sample). 3 of 5 caught.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (131 lines), index.html script, page.test.mjs, calc.test.mjs. One engine (jobCost) reused for the package table and redo sensitivity; share keys whitelisted and truncated; output escaped. Defects: readInput defaults filmCostPerFt, laborRate, bayOverheadPerDay, coatingCost, redoCost to 0 when blank with no message; CSS rules tr.break/tr.dwell/tr.off/tr.restart copied from another tool and unused (index.html:34-35); usd() duplicated in calc.mjs and index.html; techs input min=0 step=any while the engine requires an integer 1-6 (the error message covers it). Acceptable for a static tool.
evidence.claims: Checked 7 claims. Backed: disclaimer, no-warranty and no-SLA footer (page.test.mjs and read); nothing uploaded (grep finds no fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon); 'Not modelled' list matches the code; method bullets (14/24/36/70 ft, 1.0-1.5 size factors, 0/4/9 correction h) match the constants. Not backed: FAQ and JSON-LD 'The package table shows every film coverage with the coating on or off, so you can quote both' (index.html:12,122) - the table shows only the current coating choice (plan({...s, coating:'no'}) lists 4 rows, no with/without pairs); advice 'Per bay day, "Full body" earns the most ... If the bay is booked solid, sell that one first' and FAQ 'Profit per bay day shows which package to sell first' - under the tool's own cost-plus price, profit per bay day = cost per bay day x m/(1-m) exactly (checked for every package at film $24 and $8), so it ranks packages by how expensive they are per bay day, not by what they earn in a market; film and hour constants are labelled 'rules of thumb' but cite nothing.
evidence.fitness: Walked a shop owner's job: quote a full front + coating on a sedan. The tool gives a cost-plus price and film-to-buy figure in one pass, which is useful as a floor. But PPF shops price from a package menu against local competitors; there is no input for the menu or market price per package, so the 'which package to sell' output cannot answer the real question. Default install hours (14 h full front compact, 16.1 h sedan) give a 4-work-day full front with one tech, which most shops do in 1-2 days; the user can only change coating hours, not install hours per package, so a shop whose installer is faster cannot fix the 14/24/36/70 ft and 8/14/22/40 h table except via the waste % and labour rate.
evidence.domain: Margin-not-markup, waste on bought film, ceil of work days, cure days blocking the bay and an expected redo allowance are the right building blocks. Departures: (1) profit per bay day is computed from a cost-plus price, making the ranking tautological (more expensive package per day = 'earns most'); a practitioner ranks by menu price minus cost per bay day. (2) Full body sedan footage 70 x 1.15 = 80.5 ft cut (92.6 ft bought at 15% waste) vs a film supplier's guide of about 60-65 linear ft of 60 in film for a full-size sedan plus 5-10 ft spare (uppf-usa.com 'Car Wrap Vinyl Amount Guide by Vehicle Size', found by web search 2026-11-19): about 25% high before waste. (3) Install-hour table is fixed and uncited; per-package hours are not editable. (4) Flat redo cost across packages in the comparison table (a full body redo costs far more than a partial).

defects.what: 'Which package earns the most per bay day ... sell that one first' is computed from the tool's own cost-plus price, so profit per bay day = cost per bay day x m/(1-m) exactly: it ranks packages by how expensive they are per day (full body wins because it burns the most film), not by what customers pay. No input for menu or market price per package exists, so the headline advice cannot be right except by accident
FAQ and FAQPage JSON-LD claimed the package table shows every coverage 'with the coating on or off, so you can quote both'; the table shows only the current coating choice

Film footage and install-hour table (14/24/36/70 ft, 8/14/22/40 h for a compact) is uncited and not editable per package; full body sedan 80.5 ft cut vs a supplier guide of ~60-65 ft; 16.1 h full front on a sedan makes a 4-work-day job most shops do in 1-2 days
Blank film cost, labour rate, bay overhead, coating cost or redo cost silently become 0 and the job is priced without them
Headline package ranking and minimum-charge boundary are unpinned: mutants ranking by price and moving the minimum boundary both survived; only one test asserts exact dollar figures
Redo cost is one flat figure applied to every package in the comparison table, though a full body redo costs far more than a partial front
Unused CSS rules copied from another tool (tr.break, tr.dwell, tr.off, tr.restart); tech hours 24.15 display as 24.1 (float rounding)

verdict: A compact, privacy-clean cost-plus calculator whose arithmetic is right: four jobs (sample sedan $2,364.01 cost / $3,940.02 price / 5 bay days; truck full body $10,229.17; SUV coating-only $1,097.92; compact partial $1,422.33) recompute to the cent in an independent script, and it uses margin, not markup. But its headline insight is circular: profit per bay day comes from a price that is cost divided by (1 - margin), so 'which package earns the most per bay day' is just which package costs the most per day, and it tells every shop to sell full body first. Its film and hour table is uncited and not editable, runs about 25% over a supplier's full-body footage guide, and makes a full front a four-day job. The FAQ promised a coating on/off comparison the table does not give (fixed in the working tree, test added). Blank cost fields silently price as zero, and 2 of 5 seeded bugs survive, including one in the ranking. Claims, verification, fitness and domain are 2: it does not meet the bar, though everything it lists works (completeness 3).
